newsitem.title: POLAND: Optimus to form subsidiary in Ukraine.
newsitem.headline: Optimus to form subsidiary in Ukraine.

text.p: Polish computer maker Optimus SA aims to produce computer equipment in Ukraine from next month and hopes to gain a 10 percent market share there, the firm's export director said on Tuesday.

"Investment in buildings, equipment, cars and training will amount to $200,000 to $300,000 by year-end. We should gain 10 percent of the Ukrainian market. Last year we had about two to three percent," Ryszard Stefanczyk told Reuters.

He said Optimus planned to form a wholly-owned subsidiary in the Ukrainian capital of Kiev which would begin production in the second half of August and record turnover of $8-9 million by the end of the year.
Stefanczyk said Optimus' main customers in Ukraine would be large organisations.
"Our main partner is the state customs service, which has so far bought equipment worth more than $6 million. We want to introduce our offer to banks and other government agencies," Stefanczyk said.
